official.application_cycle: Next Call for Nominations - Master's Student Scholarships 2027-2029
official.status_note: The official page announces a 'Next Call for Nominations, Master's Student Scholarships 2027-2029' with submission deadline Thursday, 25 March 2027.
official.funding_period: one-off total for the MSc studies (cohort 2027-2029)
benefits: Scholarship amounting to CHF 36'000 for the Master of Science studies (previously CHF 30'000)
Mentoring opportunities offered by the SCS Foundation
Facilitated interactions with program-supporting industrial partners through the 'Meet and Greet' programme
Complimentary access to events organised by the Swiss Chemical Society
Integration support and access to the network of Alfred Werner Scholars
eligibility: BSc degree obtained from a university outside Switzerland
Wish to pursue MSc studies in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences
Admitted to a Swiss University or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology (ETH, EPFL)
Nominated by the academic institution to which the candidate has been admitted; the SCS Foundation does not accept direct applications from individual candidates
Nominations are reviewed by the Alfred Werner Fund Allocation Committee, whose members are appointed by the participating companies and academic institutions
coverage: Scholarship amounting to CHF 36'000 for the Master of Science studies
Mentoring opportunities offered by the SCS Foundation
Access to program-supporting industrial partners through Meet and Greet events
Complimentary access to events organised by the Swiss Chemical Society
application_method: Secure admission to an MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or a Swiss Federal Institute of Technology
Ask the admitting institution to submit a nomination to the SCS Foundation (direct applications are not accepted)
Nomination is reviewed by the Alfred Werner Fund Allocation Committee with members from industry and the partner universities (Basel, Bern, Geneva, Neuchatel, Zurich, EPFL, ETH)
official.application_route: Institutional nomination only - the SCS Foundation does not accept direct applications; the academic institution that admitted the candidate to the MSc submits the nomination.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency rule is published; the published eligibility rule is that the BSc degree was obtained from a university outside Switzerland.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme explicitly supports talented international students whose BSc was obtained outside Switzerland.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or a Swiss Federal Institute of Technology; supporting partners include dsm-firmenich, Givaudan, F. Hoffmann-La Roche, Merck/Sigma-Aldrich, Novartis, Syngenta and Metrohm Stiftung, and academically the Universities of Basel, Bern, Geneva, Neuchatel, Fribourg, Zurich, EPFL and ETH.
official.duration: Master of Science studies; scholarship classes are designated in two-year cohorts, e.g. 'Master's Student Scholarships 2027-2029'.
official.description: The Alfred Werner Scholarship Program of the SCS Foundation, a partner organisation of the Swiss Chemical Society, supports highly talented international students who obtained their BSc at a university outside Switzerland and wish to pursue an MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss University or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology.
official.program_type: Industry- and donor-funded master's scholarship, nomination only

verification.notes: Award amount (CHF 36'000, previously CHF 30'000) and the 25 March 2027 nomination deadline for the 2027-2029 call were read directly from the SCS Foundation Alfred Werner Scholarship page; benefits, partner universities and nomination-only procedure cross-checked on the same page plus the scholar gallery, class and Meet & Greet pages. The page publishes no statement on what the sum covers, no dossier list, and no English requirement, so those fields stay unconfirmed.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this scholarship yourself: you must first win admission to an MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at one of the partner universities (EPFL, ETH, Basel, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva or Zurich), then get that institution to nominate you to the SCS Foundation before 25 March 2027 for the 2027-2029 cohort. The practical step is to contact your department's Alfred Werner coordinator early in 2027 with your transcripts and a short motivation note, because nomination depends on the department choosing you over its other admitted candidates. The CHF 36,000 is a single total for the master's studies, not a monthly stipend, and the official page does not say whether any of it is applied to tuition, so plan to fund living costs in Switzerland largely on your own unless the Foundation confirms otherwise.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent BSc graduates from outside Switzerland with top-of-class chemistry, biochemistry or pharmaceutical sciences records who have already secured an MSc place at a partner university and can win their department's nomination.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure an MSc admission offer from EPFL, ETH, Basel, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva or Zurich before the 25 March 2027 nomination deadline, since nomination follows admission
Identify your department's Alfred Werner contact (the coordinator for each partner university is named on the SCS Foundation class pages) and email them in January or February 2027, not in March
Prepare a short nomination package to hand over: CV, final BSc transcript, admission letter and a one-page statement on why you should represent the department
Budget Swiss living costs independently - roughly CHF 1,800-2,200 per month plus health insurance and residence permit fees, figures you should confirm with the admitting university
If successful, engage early with the mentoring programme and Meet & Greet industry days, which are where the recruitment pipeline into Roche, Novartis, dsm-firmenich, Givaudan and Syngenta starts
common_rejection_risks: Sending an application straight to the SCS Foundation - submissions from individual candidates are refused outright
Holding a BSc from a Swiss university, which disqualifies you because eligibility requires the bachelor's from outside Switzerland
Pursuing an MSc outside Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences, or outside the partner institutions
Missing the department's internal nomination cut-off, which falls well before the Foundation's 25 March deadline
Assuming the CHF 36,000 pays tuition fees - the official page makes no such claim, and Swiss universities charge separate semester fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and semester fees at the Swiss university or ETH/EPFL, day-to-day living costs in Switzerland, health insurance and residence permit costs, and travel to and from Switzerland are not stated as covered by the CHF 36'000; budget for them separately and confirm current figures with the admitting university.
document_audit: No nomination dossier is published by the Foundation - ask the department's coordinator exactly what they require, typically CV, transcripts, proof of admission and a motivation letter
The foreign BSc diploma and final transcript are the core eligibility evidence; a preliminary transcript invites doubt about the 'outside Switzerland' condition
The admitting institution must have issued your admission before it can nominate you, so the MSc offer letter needs to be in hand
The Foundation publishes no language requirement, so the English rules of the admitting university's MSc programme govern your application
alerts: The 25 March 2027 date is the Foundation's nomination deadline, not yours - institutions nominate on their own earlier internal schedule
The '2027-2029' label shows the decision precedes your MSc start, so you must already hold an offer when the call closes
Cohorts are small, around seven to eight scholars per class, so the number of institutional nominations is limited and competition for them is inside your department
Older pages and third-party listings still quoting CHF 30,000 are outdated; the official amount is CHF 36'000
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admitted MSc student -> the university department nominates the candidate to the SCS Foundation before 25 March 2027 -> the Alfred Werner Fund Allocation Committee (industry and academic members) reviews the nominations -> the Foundation awards the scholarship for the 2027-2029 master's cohort, with mentoring and Meet & Greet access once studies begin.
